newsitem.title: UK: Tate shares gain after AGM statement.
newsitem.headline: Tate shares gain after AGM statement.

text.p: Shares in sugar producer Tate & Lyle Plc bounced from recent declines in early trading on Thursday after its AGM statement proved less negative on U.S. sweetener prices than some had feared.
The stock was up 6-1/2p at 433-1/2 by 0801 GMT, after yesterday touching its lowest level since July 1995.

Tate warned that profits for the first-half to March 1997 would be below last year's level, and that the strength of sterling knocked 7.1 million stg off pre-tax profits in the first quarter ended December 1996.
Even before the currency impact, it said profits were lower than last year, which had benefited from good margins in maize sweeteners in the United States.
However the announcement comes after Tate shares plummeted in recent sessions amid talk of downgrades because of pressure on high fructose corn syrup (HFCS) in the U.S.

Tate said HFCS prices remained highly competitive but "management initiatives have reduced costs and directed production towards non-HFCS products." As a result profits in dollar terms would meet earlier expectations.

The company added that favourable trends in U.S. sugar markets and reduced operating costs had resulted in higher dollar profits in the group's U.S. sugar companies compared with last year's first quarter.
"The statement wasn't as bearish as some had feared," said one senior trader.

David Lang, analyst at Henderson Crossthwaite, said there were signs that Tate's prospects were improving, pointing to the company's statement that first-half profits would be above levels in the second half of last year.
"I think the market should take comfort from that. There is a major turnaround coming," Lang said.
"If you take a long-term view you would be a buyer. The recovery is starting lower than we thought and next year could be tough, but the long-term outlook is improving."
